A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same knockout- and league-style inference-scaling research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original accuracy experiments, scaling curves, ablations, and diagnostic analyses on GPQA, MMLU-Pro-S, and MATH-500.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and reports revised and extended filtered-GPQA scaling results in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same candidate generation, knockout comparisons, and league win-rate aggregation procedures. v5's Algorithm 1 summarizes the existing league method; the anytime variants are moved to Appendix A rather than newly introduced.

E1.justification: Both evaluate GPQA's main, diamond, and extended subsets, MMLU-Pro-S, and MATH-500. Figure 3 changes filtering and candidate counts within retained GPQA coverage, without introducing another dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Figure 3 drops the standalone Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5 majority-voting comparator curves and retains only Mixed-based comparisons. Majority voting was already plotted in v3, so it is not a newly added baseline. The other reported comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 3 changes from three backends evaluated through N=64 with estimated comparison probability above 0.5 to Mixed-only evaluations through N=256 with thresholds 0.5, 0.6, and 0.7. The other stated benchmark subsets, comparison counts, decoding temperatures, and accuracy metric are retained.

E4.justification: The revised Figure 3 extends the existing assumption-validation analysis to test how stricter proxy thresholds affect scaling and saturation. The existing comparison-count and CoT ablations, opponent-subsampling analysis, and category-level diagnostics remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly discloses one full run per model/dataset combination and explains averaging results from knockout subtrees or league candidate subsamples. The checklist explicitly acknowledges absent error bars. These are new reporting details, not evidence that independent run counts increased.

E6.justification: Figure 3 substantially revises the conditional scaling evidence: for Mixed at N=64 under the stated 0.5 threshold, v3 plots approximately 90% accuracy, whereas v5 plots approximately 78%, approaching 80% at N=256. Higher-threshold curves are also added. This materially changes that diagnostic's reported scaling strength and shape; the other benchmark plots are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, two assumptions, three main theorems, complexity derivations, proofs, and four illustrative examples retain their substance. Proofs move from Appendix A to B, examples from B to C, and the agentic-workflow derivation moves into Appendix A. New explanatory remarks do not revise the formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same two algorithms, conditional exponential or power-law convergence guarantees, black-box implementation claim, and empirical scaling claims. Introductory qualifications about assumption strength do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Remark 3.2 newly discusses adversarial incorrect solutions with unusually high win rates as a failure condition for league aggregation. Section 4.1 now explicitly explains the filtered scaling plateau through the gap between empirical proxies and formal assumptions, and interprets the stricter-threshold results. Most earlier interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds an explicit link to the authors' implementation code, beyond v3's AgentScope description and upstream MMLU-Pro link. Existing model identities, temperatures, prompt templates, and positional-bias handling are retained. The PDFs establish the added access reference, not whether the linked resource is operational.

R1.justification: Remark 3.2 adds an explicit comparison between the league assumption and BoN's perfect-verifier condition, while acknowledging analogous adversarial vulnerability. The cited works otherwise match, including the retitled, published reference 4 and the reordered Qwen2.5 technical-report reference.

P1.justification: Most prose and the six-section main narrative are retained. v5 shortens the title, adds local clarifications and a checklist, removes the contents list, moves detailed future-work discussion to Appendix A, and places references before the appendices.

P2.justification: v5 comprehensively adopts NeurIPS typography, margins, and title/author formatting, resizing and repositioning displays throughout. It redraws Figure 3's right panel, adds the Algorithm 1 box and Figure 5 panel labels, and repacks appendix figures. Most underlying plotted content is reused.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves transparency and interpretation through explicit run/averaging disclosures, an implementation link, threshold-sensitivity evidence, and a concrete adversarial-failure limitation. The revised Figure 3 sacrifices the earlier backend comparison for a more informative filtering analysis. Its changed numerical values are not evidence of improved algorithm performance, and uncertainty remains unquantified; the principal gains are clearer documentation and qualification of otherwise retained research.
